task_type: production backend incident diagnosis and repair
requested_outcome: Identify and repair the causal Aurora bridge failure so accepted runtime catalogs are readable in production without relying on bundled fallback, then publish and verify the exact repair if a code release is required.
natural_destination: https://vii.spaplus.co/api/catalog for spa, vacations, events and rooms, plus the production Worker and Aurora bridge telemetry
authorization_boundary: Read production telemetry and configuration metadata, change and test repository code, and publish a reversible production repair under the user's explicit instruction. Do not expose or rotate secrets, change DNS, alter supplier records, or mutate catalog data without causal proof.

lesson_bundle.reason: The incident requires a predictive contract and evidence at the live destination, not a plausible explanation.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require competing hypotheses, a midpoint discriminating test, and live post-release evidence.

lesson_bundle.reason: A code fix or passing build does not prove the runtime catalog path recovered.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require all four catalog worlds, failure containment, persistence and rollback evidence on the exact deployed version.

lesson_bundle.reason: Diagnosis and tests may start local processes.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Track any owned processes and pass cleanup verification before delivery.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The fallback is described as fixed while the Aurora bridge still fails.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Trace the request from Worker bindings through bridge authentication and SQL execution, and require runtime source rather than bundled-fallback.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: All four production catalog responses return source runtime with current accepted generation timestamps, or the exact external blocker is proven.

predicted_rejections.rejection: A guessed secret or configuration change creates a wider outage.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Inspect configuration presence and bridge responses without exposing secrets, test one discriminating variable at a time, and keep v727 rollback available.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The repair has before-and-after bridge evidence, no secret values in artifacts, and a verified rollback identity.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Only spa is repaired while vacations, events or rooms still use stale fallback.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Treat every world sharing runtimeDatabase and callBridge as one affected family.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Production checks cover spa, vacations, events and rooms with counts, source and fetchedAt.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The bridge responds but catalog state is absent or incomplete.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Separate transport/authentication from schema/state hypotheses and inspect state and entry consistency read-only.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The supported root cause explains both the bridge telemetry and the catalog-state behavior; competing hypotheses are rejected by evidence.

affected_family: app/lib/aws-database.ts bridge transport and error handling
public catalog API for spa, vacations, events and rooms
catalog refresh and admin diagnostic routes

sources.label: VII target architecture and production truth rules
VII accepted fallback and release behavior
v727 production baseline and rollback identity

midpoint_gate.trigger: After the first read-only bridge probe and log correlation, before any production mutation or broad code edit
checks: Distinguish missing configuration from network/authentication failure and SQL/state failure
Confirm whether the same mechanism affects all four worlds
Preserve the current public fallback while diagnosing

attack_questions: Can a cold production request still fall back because callBridge fails?
Do all four worlds read the accepted runtime generation after reload?
Does a simulated bridge failure still degrade safely without exposing private errors?
Can the exact previous production version be restored without data loss?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Fresh production responses and logs tied to the deployed version, showing HTTP 200, runtime source, non-empty counts and accepted fetchedAt values.
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Focused bridge tests, full catalog regression tests, build, and production probes for spa, vacations, events and rooms.

effectiveness.baseline: v727 serves all four worlds from bundled-fallback; production logs show public_catalog_state_fallback and callBridge failures, while the precise internal bridge failure is not yet logged.
effectiveness.target: Restore runtime catalog reads in one causal repair cycle and prevent a fallback-only state from being reported as fully healthy.
